name: Best-lit spot near the pole
note: Brightest point within 20 km of the pole in NASA's LOLA illumination map (88.4% of the time over 18.6 years). Derived by us, not a named site.
source: NASA PGDA Lunar Polar Illumination, AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608

name: Shackleton crater (centre)
note: Crater floor next to the pole; permanently shadowed.

name: Mons Mouton (centre)
note: Plateau mountain between Nobile and Malapert; feature centre, not a landing point.

name: IM-2 Athena landing site
note: Where the lander came to rest, as located by LRO.
source: LROC, IM-2 Athena: A Closer View

name: IM-1 Odysseus landing site
note: Near Malapert A, as located by LRO.
source: NASA, LRO images Intuitive Machines' Odysseus lander

name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (Statio Shiv Shakti)
note: About 600 km from the pole, as located by LRO.

name: Chang'e-4, Von Kármán crater (far side)
note: Far side: Earth is never above the horizon, so there is no direct-to-Earth link. Terrain from the 1.9 km global map.

name: Apollo 11 Tranquility Base
note: Near the equator: the Sun climbs high and Earth stays high in the sky. Terrain from the 1.9 km global map.
source: NASA Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, Apollo 11
